newSounds: French u: lips say oo, tongue says ee (tu, une); nasal vowels an/en/on/in — air through the nose, no hard n; r is guttural from the back of the throat; j and g before e/i are zh like measure
rhythm: syllable-timed with the stress on the last syllable of the phrase — close to Telugu, so the rhythm is easy for you
registerFirst: vous is the polite you; keep it with strangers, officials and elders. tu is only for family, friends and children
trap: Many final letters are silent (bonjour ends in a guttural r; allez is ah-LAY, not ah-LAYZ); liaison links a hidden final consonant to the next vowel (vous allez = voo-zah-LAY)
